## Background

Tayko is a software catalog firm that sells games and educational software. It started out as a software manufacturer and later added third-party titles to its offerings. It has recently put together a revised collection of items in a new catalog, which it is preparing to roll out in a mailing.


Each catalog costs approximately $2 to mail (including printing, postage, and mailing costs). Estimate the gross profit that the firm could expect from the remaining 180,000 names if it selects them randomly from the pool.




install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_version("gains", version = "1.2")




**Step 1:** Load dataset
```{r}
Tayko.df <- read.csv("Tayko.csv",header=TRUE)
```

**Step 2:** Estimate Gross Profit
```{r}
cost_per_mail <- 2
response_rate <- 0.053
number_of_left_entries <- 180000
average_spend <- mean(Tayko.df[Tayko.df$Purchase==1,]$Spending)
gross_profit <- (average_spend * response_rate - cost_per_mail) * number_of_left_entries
gross_profit
```



Partition the data randomly into a training set (800 records), validation set (700 records), and test set (500 records).

Develop a model for classifying a customer as a purchaser or nonpurchaser (Note: Use only the training set for running the model)
We decided to attempt the following methods:

1. Step-wise logistic regression (using backward elimination)
2. Naive Bayes 
3. KNN Model
4. CART

#### Approach 1: Step-wise logistic regression (using backward elimination)

**Step 1:** Load the data and partition the data randomly into a training set (800 records), validation
set (700 records), and test set (500 records).

```{r}
Tayko.df <- read.csv("Tayko.csv",header=TRUE)
#dropping the unwanted column: last_update_days_ago and 1st_update_days_ago
Tayko.df <- Tayko.df[,-c(19,20)]

names(Tayko.df)
set.seed(6210)
all_rows <- rownames(Tayko.df)
train_rows <- sample(all_rows,800)
valid_rows <- sample(setdiff(all_rows,train_rows),700)
test_rows <- setdiff(all_rows,union(train_rows,valid_rows))

train.df <- Tayko.df[train_rows, ]
valid.df <- Tayko.df[valid_rows, ]
test.df <- Tayko.df[test_rows, ]

# Check partition sizes
cat("Training set size:", nrow(train.df), "\n")
cat("Validation set size:", nrow(valid.df), "\n")
cat("Test set size:", nrow(test.df), "\n")
```

**Step 2:** Run step-wise logistic regression using backward elimination to select
the best subset of variables

```{r}
lr_model <- glm(Purchase ~ .-Spending- sequence_number, data = train.df, family = "binomial");
lr_model_b <- step(lr_model, direction = "backward");

```
NOTE: We drop Spending because it leaks future information. At the time of mailing the catalog, Tayko would not know how much a customer will spend — only demographic and behavioral history are available. Spending and Purchase are highly correlated which could lead to incorrect high model accuracy and unrealistic predictions

**Step 3:** Create Confusion Matrixes for the validation set

**Default Cutoff (0.5) **
```{r}
#table(valid.df$Purchase)

# 1. Predict purchase probabilities on validation data
valid.prob <- predict(lr_model_b, newdata = valid.df, type = "response")

# 2. Classify purchasers vs non-purchasers with threshold 0.5
valid.class <- ifelse(valid.prob >= 0.5, 1, 0)

# 3. Confusion matrix for validation set
library(caret)
lg.cm <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(valid.class), as.factor(valid.df$Purchase), positive = "1")
print(lg.cm)
```

**What if the cut off was at 0.8?**
```{r}

# 1. Predict purchase probabilities on validation data
valid.prob1 <- predict(lr_model_b, newdata = valid.df, type = "response")

# 2. Classify purchasers vs non-purchasers with threshold 0.5
valid.class1 <- ifelse(valid.prob >= 0.8, 1, 0)

# 3. Confusion matrix for validation set
library(caret)
lg.cm1 <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(valid.class1), as.factor(valid.df$Purchase), positive = "1")
print(lg.cm1)

```

**What if the cut off was at 0.2?** 
```{r}
# 1. Predict purchase probabilities on validation data
valid.prob2 <- predict(lr_model_b, newdata = valid.df, type = "response")

# 2. Classify purchasers vs non-purchasers with threshold 0.5
valid.class2 <- ifelse(valid.prob >= 0.2, 1, 0)

# 3. Confusion matrix for validation set
library(caret)
lg.cm2 <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(valid.class2), as.factor(valid.df$Purchase), positive = "1")
print(lg.cm2)

```

**Step 4:** Plot the Lift Chart
```{r}
# Load the gains package
library(gains)

# 1. Predict probabilities on the validation set
pred.prob <- predict(lr_model_b, newdata = valid.df, type = "response")

# 2. Create the gain object
gain <- gains(actual = valid.df$Purchase, 
              predicted = pred.prob, 
              groups = 100)

# 3. Plot the Lift Chart
plot(c(0, gain$cume.pct.of.total * sum(valid.df$Purchase)) ~ c(0, gain$cume.obs),
     xlab = "# Cases", 
     ylab = "Cumulative Purchasers Captured", 
     main = "Lift Chart - Logistic Regression Model (Validation Set)",
     type = "l", 
     lwd = 2)

# 4. Add the baseline (random model)
lines(c(0, sum(valid.df$Purchase)) ~ c(0, dim(valid.df)[1]), lty = 2)
```

#### Approach 2: Naive Bayes

**Step 1:** Load the data and partition the data randomly into a training set (800 records), validation
set (700 records), and test set (500 records).

```{r}
Tayko.df <- read.csv("Tayko.csv",header=TRUE)
#dropping the unwanted column: last_update_days_ago and 1st_update_days_ago
Tayko.df <- Tayko.df[,-c(19,20)]

names(Tayko.df)
set.seed(6210)
all_rows <- rownames(Tayko.df)
train_rows <- sample(all_rows,800)
valid_rows <- sample(setdiff(all_rows,train_rows),700)
test_rows <- setdiff(all_rows,union(train_rows,valid_rows))

train.df <- Tayko.df[train_rows, ]
valid.df <- Tayko.df[valid_rows, ]
test.df <- Tayko.df[test_rows, ]

# Check partition sizes
cat("Training set size:", nrow(train.df), "\n")
cat("Validation set size:", nrow(valid.df), "\n")
cat("Test set size:", nrow(test.df), "\n")
```

**Step 2:** Build Naive Bayes model on training set

```{r}
# 0. Drop 'Spending' from training and validation sets (if not already done)
train.nb <- train.df[ , !(names(train.df) %in% c("Spending", "sequence_number")) ]
valid.nb <- valid.df[ , !(names(valid.df) %in% c("Spending", "sequence_number")) ]

# 1. Build Naive Bayes model on training set
library(e1071)
nb_model <- naiveBayes(factor(Purchase) ~ ., data = train.nb)
nb_model

```

**Step 3:** Predict probabilities on validation set
```{r}
nb_valid.prob <- predict(nb_model, newdata = valid.nb, type = "raw")[,2]  # Get probability for purchaser (class 1)
```

**Step 4:** Confusion Matrix on validation set
```{r}
library(caret)

# Classify using 0.5 threshold
nb_valid.class <- ifelse(nb_valid.prob >= 0.5, 1, 0)
nb.cm <- confusionMatrix(factor(nb_valid.class),factor(valid.nb$Purchase), positive = "1")
print(nb.cm)
```

**Step 5**: Plot The Lift Chart
```{r}
library(gains)

nb_gain <- gains(actual = valid.nb$Purchase, predicted = nb_valid.prob, groups = 100)

plot(c(0, nb_gain$cume.pct.of.total * sum(valid.nb$Purchase)) ~ c(0, nb_gain$cume.obs),
     xlab = "# Cases", 
     ylab = "Cumulative Purchasers Captured", 
     main = "Lift Chart - Naive Bayes Model (Validation Set)",
     type = "l", 
     lwd = 2)

lines(c(0, sum(valid.nb$Purchase)) ~ c(0, dim(valid.nb)[1]), lty = 2)
```

#### Approach 3: KNN Model

**Step 1:** Load the data and partition the data randomly into a training set (800 records), validation
set (700 records), and test set (500 records).

```{r}
Tayko.df <- read.csv("Tayko.csv",header=TRUE)
names(Tayko.df)
set.seed(6210)
all_rows <- rownames(Tayko.df)
train_rows <- sample(all_rows,800)
valid_rows <- sample(setdiff(all_rows,train_rows),700)
test_rows <- setdiff(all_rows,union(train_rows,valid_rows))

train.df <- Tayko.df[train_rows, ]
valid.df <- Tayko.df[valid_rows, ]
test.df <- Tayko.df[test_rows, ]

# Check partition sizes
cat("Training set size:", nrow(train.df), "\n")
cat("Validation set size:", nrow(valid.df), "\n")
cat("Test set size:", nrow(test.df), "\n")
```

**Step 2:** Normalize Necessary Columns
```{r}
train.norm <- train.df
valid.norm <- valid.df
full.norm <- Tayko.df

predictor.cols <- setdiff(names(Tayko.df), c("Purchase", "Spending", "sequence_number"))

norm.values <- preProcess(train.df[, predictor.cols], method=c("center", "scale"))

train.norm[, predictor.cols] <- predict(norm.values, train.df[, predictor.cols])
valid.norm[, predictor.cols] <- predict(norm.values, valid.df[, predictor.cols])
full.norm[, predictor.cols]  <- predict(norm.values, Tayko.df[, predictor.cols])

```

**Step 3:** Find the best K-Value
```{r}

library(FNN)
# Prepare to store accuracy for each value of k
accuracy.df <- data.frame(k =1:20, accuracy = rep(0, 20))

# Loop over k values from 1 to 20
for (i in 1:20) {
  knn.pred <- knn(train = train.norm[, predictor.cols],  
                  test  = valid.norm[, predictor.cols],
                  cl    = train.norm$Purchase,
                  k     = i)
  
# store the accuracy
accuracy.df[i, 2] <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(knn.pred),as.factor(valid.norm$Purchase))$overall["Accuracy"]
}

#store theaccuracy table
print(accuracy.df)

```

**Step 4:** Display Confusion Matrix
```{r}
optimal.k <- 3

# Generate predictions for the validation set using k = 3
knn.pred <- knn(train = train.norm[, predictor.cols],
                test  = valid.norm[, predictor.cols],
                cl    = train.norm$Purchase,
                k     = optimal.k)

# Display full confusion matrix
knn.cm <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(knn.pred),
                as.factor(valid.norm$Purchase),
                positive = "1")

print(knn.cm)

```

#### Approach #4: CART

**Step 1:** Load the data and partition the data randomly into a training set (800 records), validation
set (700 records), and test set (500 records).

```{r}
Tayko.df <- read.csv("Tayko.csv",header=TRUE)

# Eliminate "sequence_number" & "Spending" variable. "Spending" is related(homogeneous) to the "Purchase" column, potentially leading to overfitting.
Tayko.df <- read.csv("Tayko.csv",header=TRUE)
Tayko.df <- Tayko.df[ , -c(1,19,20,25)]
head(Tayko.df)

set.seed(6210)

full_rows <- nrow(Tayko.df)

training_rows <- sample(full_rows, 800)
validation_rows <- sample(setdiff(full_rows, training_rows), 700)
test_rows <- sample(setdiff(full_rows, union(training_rows,validation_rows)), 500)
```

**Step 2:** Scale necessary columns
```{r}
# scale freq and spending field
columns_to_scale <- c("Freq")
Tayko.df[columns_to_scale] <- scale(Tayko.df[columns_to_scale])

dim(Tayko.df)
head(Tayko.df)
```

**Step 3:** Define and plot tree
```{r}
# CART Model --- IMPURE TERMINAL NODES DUE TO MIX OF CLASSES IN THE NODES
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)

# Subset the data
training.df <- Tayko.df[training_rows, ]
validation.df <- Tayko.df[validation_rows, ]
test.df <- Tayko.df[test_rows, ]

# Define the tree
train_ct <- rpart(Purchase ~ ., data = training.df, method = "class")

# Plot the tree
prp(train_ct, type = 1, extra = 1, under = TRUE, split.font = 1, varlen = -10,
   box.col=ifelse(train_ct$frame$var == "<leaf>", 'gray', 'white'))
```

FULL GROWN TREE where cp = 0 to process until it reaches pure leaves
```{r}

# Define the tree
pure_ct <- rpart(Purchase ~ ., data = training.df, method = "class", cp = 0, minsplit = 1)

# Count the number of leaves
length(pure_ct$frame$var[pure_ct$frame$var == "<leaf>"])

# Plot the tree
prp(pure_ct, type = 1, extra = 1, under = TRUE, split.font = 1, varlen = -10,
   box.col=ifelse(train_ct$frame$var == "<leaf>", 'gray', 'white'))
```

**Step 3:** Show confusion matrices and accurarcy for Default and Full Trees
```{r}
# Confusion Matrices and Accuracy for the Default and Full trees
default.ct.point.pred.train <- predict(train_ct, training.df, type = "class")

library(caret)
confusionMatrix(default.ct.point.pred.train, as.factor(training.df$Purchase), positive = "1")
```

**Step 4:** Prune for most optimal complexity
```{r}
# CART MODEL --- Pruning for most optimal complexity
optimal_ct <- rpart(Purchase ~ ., data = training.df, method ="class",
                    cp = 0.00001, minsplit = 5, xval = 5)

printcp(optimal_ct) # used to identify the most optimal ct with the lowest error
```

```{r}
# CART MODEL --- Most optimal pruned model
pruned_ct <- prune(optimal_ct, 
                   cp = optimal_ct$cptable[which.min(optimal_ct$cptable[,"xerror"]),"CP"])

length(pruned_ct$frame$var[pruned_ct$frame$var == "<leaf>"])

prp(pruned_ct, type = 1, extra = 1, split.font = 1, varlen = -10,
    box.col=ifelse(pruned_ct$frame$var == "<leaf>", 'gray', 'white'))

# Predict on the validation set using the pruned tree
pruned.pred <- predict(pruned_ct, newdata = validation.df, type = "class")

# Display the confusion matrix
cart_pruned.cm <- confusionMatrix(pruned.pred, as.factor(validation.df$Purchase), positive = "1")
print(cart_pruned.cm)


```


#### Final Results

```{r}

# Extract metrics
model.names <- c("Logistic Regression", "Naive Bayes", "KNN", "CART (Pruned)")

accuracy <- c(lg.cm$overall["Accuracy"],
              nb.cm$overall["Accuracy"],
              knn.cm$overall["Accuracy"],
              cart_pruned.cm$overall["Accuracy"])

sensitivity <- c(lg.cm$byClass["Sensitivity"],
                 nb.cm$byClass["Sensitivity"],
                 knn.cm$byClass["Sensitivity"],
                 cart_pruned.cm$byClass["Sensitivity"])

specificity <- c(lg.cm$byClass["Specificity"],
                 nb.cm$byClass["Specificity"],
                 knn.cm$byClass["Specificity"],
                 cart_pruned.cm$byClass["Specificity"])

# Create summary data frame
comparison.df <- data.frame(
  Model = model.names,
  Accuracy = round(accuracy, 3),
  Sensitivity = round(sensitivity, 3),
  Specificity = round(specificity, 3)
)

print(comparison.df)


```


Develop a model for predicting spending among the purchasers.
Create a vector of ID’s of only purchasers’ records (Purchase = 1).
Partition this dataset into the training and validation records. (Use the same training/validation labels from earlier)

Develop models for predicting spending. We decided to try to following:

1. Multiple Linear Regression (using stepwise regression)
2. Regression trees
3. Neural Network Analysis

#### Multiple Linear Regression (using stepwise regression)

**Step 1:** Load the data and partition the data randomly into a training set (800 records), validation
set (700 records), and test set (500 records).

```{r}
Tayko.df <- read.csv("Tayko.csv",header=TRUE)
#dropping the unwanted column: last_update_days_ago and 1st_update_days_ago
Tayko.df <- Tayko.df[,-c(19,20)]

names(Tayko.df)
set.seed(6210)
all_rows <- rownames(Tayko.df)
train_rows <- sample(all_rows,800)
valid_rows <- sample(setdiff(all_rows,train_rows),700)
test_rows <- setdiff(all_rows,union(train_rows,valid_rows))

train.df <- Tayko.df[train_rows, ]
valid.df <- Tayko.df[valid_rows, ]
test.df <- Tayko.df[test_rows, ]

# Check partition sizes
cat("Training set size:", nrow(train.df), "\n")
cat("Validation set size:", nrow(valid.df), "\n")
cat("Test set size:", nrow(test.df), "\n")
```

**Step 2:** Scale necessary columns
```{r}
# scale freq and spending field
columns_to_scale <- c("Freq", "Spending")
Tayko.df[columns_to_scale] <- scale(Tayko.df[columns_to_scale])

dim(Tayko.df)
head(Tayko.df)
```


**Step 3**: Build linear regression model
```{r}

# Build linear regression model
lm.model <- lm(Spending ~ ., data = train.df)

# View summary (optional, shows significant predictors)
summary(lm.model)
```

**Step 4**: Predict using validation set
```{r}
# Predict Spending for validation set
lm.pred <- predict(lm.model, newdata = valid.df)
```

#### Approach 2: Regression trees

**Step 1:** Load the data and partition the data randomly into a training set (800 records), validation
set (700 records), and test set (500 records).

```{r}
Tayko.df <- read.csv("Tayko.csv",header=TRUE)
#dropping the unwanted column: last_update_days_ago and 1st_update_days_ago
Tayko.df <- Tayko.df[,-c(19,20)]

names(Tayko.df)
set.seed(6210)
all_rows <- rownames(Tayko.df)
train_rows <- sample(all_rows,800)
valid_rows <- sample(setdiff(all_rows,train_rows),700)
test_rows <- setdiff(all_rows,union(train_rows,valid_rows))

train.df <- Tayko.df[train_rows, ]
valid.df <- Tayko.df[valid_rows, ]
test.df <- Tayko.df[test_rows, ]

# Check partition sizes
cat("Training set size:", nrow(train.df), "\n")
cat("Validation set size:", nrow(valid.df), "\n")
cat("Test set size:", nrow(test.df), "\n")
```

**Step 2:** Scale necessary columns
```{r}
# scale freq and spending field
columns_to_scale <- c("Freq", "Spending")
Tayko.df[columns_to_scale] <- scale(Tayko.df[columns_to_scale])

dim(Tayko.df)
head(Tayko.df)
```

**Step 3**: Build and plot regression tree
```{r}
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(forecast)

# Regression tree
reg.tree <- rpart(Spending ~ ., data = train.df, method = "anova")
```

**Step 4**: Plot the tree
```{r}
# Plot tree
prp(reg.tree, type = 1, extra = 101, under = TRUE, split.font = 1, varlen = -10)
```

**Step 5**: Predict using validation set
```{r}
# Predict Spending for validation set
tree.pred <- predict(reg.tree, newdata = valid.df)

options(scipen=999, digits = 3)
accuracy(tree.pred, valid.df$Spending)
r2 <- cor(tree.pred, valid.df$Spending)^2
print(r2)

```

#### Approach 3: Neural Network Analysis

**Step 1:** Load the data and partition the data randomly into a training set (800 records), validation
set (700 records), and test set (500 records).

```{r}
Tayko.df <- read.csv("Tayko.csv",header=TRUE)
#dropping the unwanted column: last_update_days_ago and 1st_update_days_ago
Tayko.df <- Tayko.df[,-c(19,20)]

names(Tayko.df)
set.seed(6210)
all_rows <- rownames(Tayko.df)
train_rows <- sample(all_rows,800)
valid_rows <- sample(setdiff(all_rows,train_rows),700)
test_rows <- setdiff(all_rows,union(train_rows,valid_rows))

train.df <- Tayko.df[train_rows, ]
valid.df <- Tayko.df[valid_rows, ]
test.df <- Tayko.df[test_rows, ]

# Check partition sizes
cat("Training set size:", nrow(train.df), "\n")
cat("Validation set size:", nrow(valid.df), "\n")
cat("Test set size:", nrow(test.df), "\n")
```

**Step 2:** Scale necessary columns
```{r}
# scale freq and spending field
columns_to_scale <- c("Freq", "Spending")
Tayko.df[columns_to_scale] <- scale(Tayko.df[columns_to_scale])

dim(Tayko.df)
head(Tayko.df)
```

**Step 3: Create Neural Network**
```{r}
library(neuralnet)
library(caret)
library(scales)

nn <- neuralnet(Spending ~ .,
                data = train.df, linear.output = FALSE, hidden = c(3, 3), 
                threshold=0.01)

plot(nn, rep="best")

nn.results <- compute(nn, valid.df)
```

#### Final Results

```{r}
# Get R-squared for each model
lm.r2 <- cor(lm.pred, valid.df$Spending)^2
tree.r2 <- cor(tree.pred, valid.df$Spending)^2

# For neural network, get prediction on validation data
nn.pred <- compute(nn, valid.df)$net.result
nn.r2 <- cor(nn.pred, valid.df$Spending)^2

# Compute RMSE and MAE for each model
lm.rmse <- sqrt(mean((lm.pred - valid.df$Spending)^2))
tree.rmse <- sqrt(mean((tree.pred - valid.df$Spending)^2))
nn.rmse <- sqrt(mean((nn.pred - valid.df$Spending)^2))

lm.mae <- mean(abs(lm.pred - valid.df$Spending))
tree.mae <- mean(abs(tree.pred - valid.df$Spending))
nn.mae <- mean(abs(nn.pred - valid.df$Spending))

# Create expanded summary data frame
model.summary <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Linear Regression", "Regression Tree", "Neural Network"),
  R_squared = round(c(lm.r2, tree.r2, nn.r2), 3),
  RMSE = round(c(lm.rmse, tree.rmse, nn.rmse), 2),
  MAE = round(c(lm.mae, tree.mae, nn.mae), 2)
)

print(model.summary)

```
